newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industrial employment down 0.2 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industrial employment down 0.2 pct in June.

text.p: Employment levels in Brazil's industrial sector fell 0.2 percent in June from May, the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said in a statement.
In the two years since Brazil introduced its economic stabilization Real Plan the industrial sector has seen an 11 percent reduction in its manual labor force, the IBGE said.

The IBGE said June's figure reflected a fall in industrial employment in the south of the country and Minas Gerais state. Industrial employment levels in Sao Paulo remained stable in June, while Rio de Janeiro and states in the northeast of Brazil increased the number of jobs in industry, it added.
The tobacco sector experienced the greatest number of job losses in June, down 14.2 percent.

In the first half of 1996, industrial employment fell in all areas of Brazil, with Sao Paulo state recording the largest fall at 14.7 percent, followed by the south of Brazil with a decline of 11.4 percent, the IBGE said.
Salaries paid in June also decreased, down one percent from May and 10 percent from June last year, according to the IBGE.
Total hours worked in the industrial sector increased 1.4 percent in May compared with April, but fell 0.9 percent compared with May 1995, the IBGE said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
